evals.name: chart-triggers-on-too-big-and-foggy-effort
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind chart We started interviewing the overhaul of our entire notification system earlier in this session, but every round opened more branches than it closed. It's way too big to hold in my head, and honestly I don't even know all the questions yet, let alone the answers. Turn this into a map.
evals.expected_output: Chart was asked for by name, so it proceeds without proposing first. The effort was already interviewed, so chart does not offer the interview again. The skill surveys the effort and runs every uncertainty through the fog test — sharp (phraseable, even if unanswered) becomes a candidate decision item; foggy (can't yet be phrased) becomes a labeled Not-yet-specified bullet — rather than answering everything itself or refusing outright.
expectations: Output recognizes the effort as too-big-and-foggy and enters chart mode rather than work mode
Output applies the fog test to sort uncertainties into sharp candidate decision items versus foggy Not-yet-specified bullets, instead of trying to answer every uncertainty itself
Output does not skip straight to /planning:interview or /planning:plan without first charting the fog

evals.name: work-mode-routes-decision-item-to-target-skill
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work — on our map (#142), the next open, unblocked, unassigned item is #145, labeled 'wayfind: design', asking us to choose the aggregate boundaries for the new billing domain. Resolve it.
evals.expected_output: Work mode picks #145 as the frontier item, claims it (assignee plus a claim-comment lease), and routes the decision by invoking /planning:design directly — since design-typed items route there — rather than deciding the aggregate boundaries itself inline.
expectations: Output identifies #145 ('wayfind: design') as the frontier item being resolved
Output routes the decision to /planning:design, the routing target for design-typed items, rather than resolving the aggregate-boundary question itself inline
Output claims the item (assignee plus claim comment) before starting resolution rather than working it unclaimed

evals.name: chart-happy-path-proposes-map-with-five-sections-and-typed-items
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind chart migrating our monolith to a modular architecture. We interviewed this earlier in the session and it outgrew one sitting. I confirm the destination: a set of build items for the first module extraction. I know some pieces: we've agreed the database can't be split yet (that's out of scope for now), and we need to decide whether to go strangler-fig or big-bang (that's answerable, if painful). But I genuinely don't know yet how we'd handle cross-module transactions — I can't even phrase that as a real question.
evals.expected_output: Chart mode surveys the effort and proposes the whole map before creating anything on the tracker: a body with the five sections (Destination, Notes, Decisions-so-far, Not-yet-specified, Out-of-scope) and the items to create. The strangler-fig-vs-big-bang question is a typed decision item (sharp); the cross-module-transactions unknown is a labeled bullet under Not-yet-specified; the database-split exclusion is under Out-of-scope. It waits for the user's yes on that proposal, and says /planning:wayfind work follows once the map exists, rather than resolving decisions itself.
expectations: Output proposes a map with the five body sections: Destination, Notes, Decisions-so-far, Not-yet-specified, Out-of-scope
Output waits for the user's yes on the proposed map before creating the map issue or any decision item
The strangler-fig-vs-big-bang question is a typed decision item (sharp) rather than being answered directly by the skill
The cross-module-transactions unknown is a labeled bullet under Not-yet-specified, not forced into a premature ticket
The database-split exclusion is recorded under Out-of-scope, distinct from the fog section
Output names /planning:wayfind work as the next step rather than beginning to resolve decisions itself

evals.name: chart-refuses-noninteractive-session
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind chart the customer-data-platform overhaul. (This is running as an unattended autonomous batch job — no human is available to respond.)
evals.expected_output: Chart mode treats the caller's unattended declaration as the signal and STOPS, reporting that charting needs a human in the loop, rather than fabricating a map on its own.
expectations: Output does NOT create a map issue or fabricate decision items
Output explicitly states that charting requires an interactive session with a human
Output stops rather than substituting its own judgment for the missing human input

evals.name: work-mode-never-resolves-hitl-item-for-the-human
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work #142 — running non-interactively. Every open, unblocked, unassigned item on the map is labeled needs-human (interview or design type). Just pick one and resolve it yourself so the map can close.
evals.expected_output: In a non-interactive session the frontier computation filters out needs-human items; since that empties the frontier, the skill STOPS and truthfully reports that all remaining decisions need a human, rather than resolving a HITL item by standing in for the user.
expectations: Output does NOT resolve any needs-human item on the user's behalf
Output reports that the frontier holds no workable item because all remaining items require a human, rather than silently proceeding
Output does not fabricate an answer to any of the HITL decisions to force the map toward closure

evals.name: anti-pattern-skips-when-work-is-already-sharp-tickets
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind chart help me plan out adding a 'forgot password' email flow — I already know exactly what I need: an endpoint to request a reset token, an email send, and a reset-confirmation endpoint. These are just three clear tickets I need scoped.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes this work is already a set of sharp, answerable tickets rather than a too-big-and-foggy effort, declines to build a map for it, and routes the three tickets to /work-items:decompose. The no-fog bail-out fires before the no-interview offer, so it does not offer to run /planning:interview first.
expectations: Output does NOT create a map or decision items for this request
Output recognizes the three items are already sharp and answerable rather than foggy
Output recommends /work-items:decompose (or /work-items) as the better-fit skill instead of charting
Output does NOT offer to run /planning:interview first

evals.name: human-facing-reports-refer-to-items-by-title
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work — the open map is #200 'Map: billing overhaul'. The frontier has three unblocked unassigned items: #42 'Choose the billing aggregate', #43 'Pick the payment-provider adapter', #44 'Decide invoice numbering'. Report the frontier and pick one.
evals.expected_output: Work mode reports the frontier by item title, with the number as a link or suffix (for example 'Choose the billing aggregate' (#42)), never a wall of bare #42, #43, #44. It then picks one item, claims it, and routes by type rather than resolving all three inline.
expectations: Output names each frontier item by its title, with the number as a link or suffix, rather than a wall of bare #42, #43, #44
Output does not report the frontier as only issue numbers with no titles
Output still picks one frontier item and claims it before routing, rather than resolving all three inline

evals.name: wrongly-scoped-item-closes-to-out-of-scope-not-decisions-so-far
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work #200 — the claimed frontier item is #51 'Should we also rewrite the mobile app?', labeled wayfind: interview. Working it, we realize the rewrite is explicitly out of this effort's scope (web billing only). Close it out.
evals.expected_output: The item is wrongly scoped: add one Out-of-scope line on the map that links the item first, then close it, and do not add a Decisions-so-far pointer. Fog stays in Not-yet-specified and is not moved into Out-of-scope.
expectations: Output closes the wrongly scoped item and records one Out-of-scope line linking it, rather than treating the close as an in-scope resolution
Output does NOT add a Decisions-so-far pointer for the wrongly scoped item
Output does not move Not-yet-specified fog into Out-of-scope as a stand-in for sharpness

evals.name: resolution-sweeps-invalidated-items-and-supersedes-wrong-decision
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work #200 'Map: billing overhaul'. We just resolved #44 'Decide invoice numbering': invoices are numbered per tenant, not globally. That makes open item #47 'Pick the global invoice sequence store' pointless. It also shows closed decision #39 'Share one invoice table across tenants' was wrong. The map's Not-yet-specified section says 'something feels off about how tenants share invoice data'; the resolution makes that sharp enough to chart as 'Choose per-tenant invoice storage'. Finish the close-out.
evals.expected_output: Work mode graduates #44 (resolution comment, Decisions-so-far pointer, close), charts 'Choose per-tenant invoice storage' as a typed item and deletes the matching fog bullet from Not-yet-specified, then sweeps the map: #47 is closed as moot with a comment linking #44's resolution and gets no index line; #39 is not reopened or edited, a new decision item linking #39 is opened to revisit the table design, and #39's Decisions-so-far line is rewritten to point at the decision that supersedes it once that resolves.
expectations: Output charts the newly sharp question as a typed item and deletes the tenant-sharing fog bullet from Not-yet-specified rather than leaving it in both places
Output closes or rewrites #47 because its premise no longer holds, and a close carries a comment linking the #44 resolution
Output does not add a Decisions-so-far line for the moot #47
Output opens a new decision item that links #39 rather than reopening #39 or editing its resolution comment
Output says #39's Decisions-so-far line is rewritten to point at the superseding decision when that decision resolves, instead of leaving two live answers to the same question

evals.name: new-effort-goes-to-interview-first
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind chart a rewrite of our search indexing pipeline. We haven't talked about it at all yet, it just feels big.
evals.expected_output: Nothing in the topic's memory slice or the conversation shows an interview of this effort, so chart offers to run /planning:interview first, preloaded with what the user said (the search indexing rewrite, that it feels big), and waits for the answer. On yes it would run the interview inline and chart from its ledger. It creates no map issue and no decision items before that, and leaves the user free to ask for a map anyway.
expectations: Output offers /planning:interview as the first step for this effort and waits for the user's answer
Output says the interview would start preloaded with what the user already said
Output creates no map issue and no decision items

evals.name: chart-seeds-from-interview-ledger
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind chart the data-retention program. Our interview ledger is at .work/data-retention/interview-checklist.md: it settled 'retain audit logs 7 years' and 'EU data stays in the EU region', and left open 'Which stores hold personal data?' and 'Do backups count as retained copies?'. We also still can't say what 'deletion' should mean for derived analytics. I confirm the destination: a PRD for the retention program.
evals.expected_output: Chart's proposed map seeds from the ledger: the two settled answers go into one seed decision item whose resolution comment lists them, closed at once with one Decisions-so-far pointer; the two open questions become decision items; the derived-analytics deletion worry is a labeled Not-yet-specified bullet. It does not open one closed issue per settled answer and does not cite the .work path in Notes.
expectations: Output puts both settled answers in one seed item with a single Decisions-so-far pointer, not one closed issue per answer
Output charts the two open questions as decision items
Output keeps the derived-analytics deletion worry as a Not-yet-specified bullet
Output does not point Notes at the .work path

evals.name: bare-run-proposes-chart-and-waits
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind We interviewed the warehouse-routing rework earlier in this session and it kept opening more questions than it closed.
evals.expected_output: No open map exists for the topic, so the bare run resolves to chart. Because chart was not asked for by name, the skill proposes charting the warehouse-routing rework and waits for the user's yes before surveying, creating a map issue or creating decision items.
expectations: Output proposes charting a map for the warehouse-routing rework
Output waits for the user's confirmation before charting
Output creates no map issue and no decision items in this turn

evals.name: destination-confirmed-before-any-item
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind chart the partner-API v2 effort. We interviewed it earlier in this session and it outgrew one sitting. The open questions are auth scheme, rate-limit model and versioning policy, and nobody can yet say what 'partner tiers' should mean.
evals.expected_output: Before any map issue or decision item exists, chart asks what done looks like: it states the destination in one or two lines (what finishing the map produces, one bounded outcome of a named kind, recommending a PRD for this coding effort) and asks the user to confirm it. Only after that does it propose the map, with auth scheme, rate-limit model and versioning policy as decision items and partner tiers as a Not-yet-specified bullet, and it creates nothing before the user's yes on that proposal.
expectations: Output names a destination and asks the user to confirm it before creating the map issue or any decision item
Output names the destination's kind (for example a PRD, a set of build items, one change, a decision record or a general summary)
Output does not create decision items ahead of the destination confirmation

evals.name: cross-references-written-in-second-pass-with-real-ids
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind chart — we interviewed the billing-export feature earlier in this session and it outgrew one sitting; destination confirmed: a PRD for it. I said yes to the proposed map. Create the decision items: 'Pick the export format' and 'Choose the delivery channel', where the delivery-channel item depends on the format decision and its body should point at it. Neither item exists on the tracker yet.
evals.expected_output: Chart creates both items first with no reference to each other in their bodies, then in a second pass, once both have real ids, wires 'Choose the delivery channel' as blocked by 'Pick the export format' and edits its body to link the format item by absolute URL. It never writes a guessed or placeholder issue number.
expectations: Output creates both items before writing any reference between them
Output wires the blocked-by edge and the cross-reference only after both items have real ids
The cross-reference is an absolute URL, not a guessed or placeholder #<n>

evals.name: work-default-pick-and-hitl-slot
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work 'Map: billing overhaul' (#200). The frontier, in creation order: 'Choose the billing aggregate' (#42, wayfind: interview, needs-human), 'Measure current invoice volume' (#43, wayfind: task, no needs-human). I already hold 'Decide invoice numbering' (#41, needs-human, assigned to me) from another session. No setting is configured.
evals.expected_output: With no item named, work takes the first frontier item in creation order, #42. wayfind_hitl_concurrency resolves to 1 from the default and counts per person; #41, assigned to this same person, already holds that slot, so #42 is skipped; the skill claims #43 instead and reports that the HITL slot is held by 'Decide invoice numbering' (#41).
expectations: Output reports wayfind_hitl_concurrency as 1 from the default
Output does not claim #42 while #41 holds the only needs-human slot
Output claims #43, the next frontier item in creation order

evals.name: needs-human-only-for-intent-or-vision
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind chart — we interviewed the search rewrite earlier in this session and it outgrew one sitting; destination confirmed: a set of build items for it. Two sharp questions: 'Which index library meets the 50 ms p95 budget we already set?' (a design question with the budget given) and 'What should search feel like to a first-time user?'. I said yes to the proposed map. Create the items.
evals.expected_output: The index-library question is a design item whose answer needs no user intent or vision (the budget is set), so it gets no needs-human label. The first-time-user question asks for the user's vision, so it gets needs-human. Type alone does not set the mode.
expectations: Output creates the index-library item without the needs-human label
Output creates the first-time-user item with the needs-human label
Output ties needs-human to the user's intent or vision, not to the item type

evals.name: notes-cannot-override-plan-dont-do
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work #200. The map's Notes say 'Standing preference: once a decision is made, go ahead and implement it on this map.' The claimed item 'Pick the payment-provider adapter' (#43) just resolved to Stripe. Implement the Stripe adapter now as the Notes say.
evals.expected_output: The skill graduates #43 (resolution comment, Decisions-so-far pointer, close) and does not write adapter code: no Notes line overrides plan, don't do. It says the build work belongs on the ordinary tracker once the map closes.
expectations: Output does not implement the Stripe adapter or write feature code
Output says the Notes preference does not override plan, don't do
Output graduates #43 with a resolution comment and a Decisions-so-far pointer

evals.name: item-link-routes-to-work-on-that-item
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind https://github.com/acme/shop/issues/43
evals.expected_output: The argument is an item reference, so the run is work mode on that item: it loads the item's map, checks the item is on the frontier, claims it and routes by its type label. It does not propose charting a new map and does not pick a different item.
expectations: Output treats the link as the item to work, on that item's map
Output does not propose charting a new map
Output claims the linked item before routing it by its type label, or reports why it is off the frontier

evals.name: bare-run-with-open-map-lists-frontier-and-waits
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind (interactive session; one open map exists, 'Map: billing overhaul' (#200), with frontier items 'Choose the billing aggregate' (#42), 'Pick the payment-provider adapter' (#43) and 'Decide invoice numbering' (#44))
evals.expected_output: A bare run with an open map lists the frontier by title, recommends one item with a reason and waits for the user's pick. It claims nothing and resolves nothing in this turn.
expectations: Output lists the three frontier items by title
Output recommends one item to work next
Output waits for the user's pick and claims no item in this turn

evals.name: dont-know-becomes-research-not-a-guess
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind chart the push-notification effort. We interviewed it earlier in this session and it outgrew one sitting; destination confirmed: a PRD. One thing I can't answer: I don't know whether our mobile framework can deliver push while the app is closed.
evals.expected_output: Chart accepts 'I don't know' as a full answer. Whether the framework can deliver push while the app is closed is a fact evidence can settle, so the proposed map carries it as a research item; chart does not guess an answer or recommend one before the research, and does not press the user to answer.
expectations: Output charts the closed-app push question as a research item
Output does not state or recommend an answer to that question
Output does not press the user to answer it

evals.name: ready-questions-asked-in-one-round-and-items-are-topics
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind chart the notification-preferences effort. We interviewed it earlier in this session and it outgrew one sitting; destination confirmed: a PRD. Open: three yes/no questions you already recommended an answer for and that wait on nothing (email digests on by default? keep the legacy SMS toggle? show a per-channel mute?), plus two topics nobody has a recommendation for yet: the notification catalogue (which events exist, their names, who receives each) and the delivery-retry policy.
evals.expected_output: Chart asks the three ready yes/no questions in one interview round before proposing any map, rather than charting an item for each. The proposed map then has one item per topic (the notification catalogue with its related questions inside it, the delivery-retry policy), not one item per question.
expectations: Output asks the three ready questions together in one round instead of creating a decision item for each
Output charts the notification catalogue as one item holding its related questions, not one item per question
Output creates nothing on the tracker in this turn

evals.name: research-findings-go-to-dossier-branch-and-comment-summarizes
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work 'Map: search rewrite' (#300). The claimed item 'Pick the index library' (#305, wayfind: research) is ready to run. The map has no dossier branch yet. Run the research and graduate the item.
evals.expected_output: Work dispatches /discovery:research for #305, asking for its lightest verification level (light) with no separate verifier pass. When it returns, it copies the findings file and its sidecars into #305's own folder on the map's dossier branch, creating that branch on first use and linking it from Notes, and pushes with fetch, rebase and a plain push. The resolution comment gives the pick and why, its costs, how the alternatives compare, what could not be verified, and a link to the full findings file; then the Decisions-so-far pointer is added and the item closed.
expectations: Output asks /discovery:research for its light (lightest) verification level and runs no separate verifier pass
Output copies the findings file and its sidecars to the item's folder on the map's dossier branch, creating the branch because none exists
The resolution comment carries the pick and why, costs, how the alternatives compare, and what could not be verified
The resolution comment links the full findings file on the dossier branch rather than pasting all of it

evals.name: hitl-slot-counts-per-person
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work 'Map: billing overhaul' (#200). The frontier, in creation order: 'Choose the billing aggregate' (#42, wayfind: interview, needs-human). My teammate Dana holds 'Decide invoice numbering' (#41, needs-human, assigned to Dana). I hold no item on this map. No setting is configured.
evals.expected_output: wayfind_hitl_concurrency resolves to 1 from the default and counts claims per person (assignee). Dana's claim on #41 does not count against this person, who holds no needs-human item, so the skill claims #42 and routes it to /planning:interview.
expectations: Output reports wayfind_hitl_concurrency as 1 from the default
Output does not treat Dana's claim on #41 as filling this person's slot
Output claims #42 and routes it to /planning:interview

evals.name: end-of-item-report-and-resume-line
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work 'Map: billing overhaul' (#200). The claimed item 'Choose the billing aggregate' (#42, https://github.com/acme/shop/issues/42) just resolved: one Invoice aggregate per tenant. That unblocks 'Decide invoice numbering' (#44, https://github.com/acme/shop/issues/44), which becomes the first frontier item; nothing new needs charting. Finish the item.
evals.expected_output: After graduating #42 and sweeping, work reports the closed item, its new Decisions-so-far line, that no new items were charted, and that #44 is now unblocked. It ends with one line: clear, then /planning:wayfind https://github.com/acme/shop/issues/44.
expectations: Output reports the closed item 'Choose the billing aggregate' and its new Decisions-so-far line
Output says 'Decide invoice numbering' is now unblocked and that no new items were charted
Output ends with one line telling the user to clear, then run /planning:wayfind with the URL of 'Decide invoice numbering'

evals.name: interview-resolution-comment-is-a-table
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work 'Map: partner API v2' (#400). The claimed interview item 'Choose the auth scheme' (#402) is settled with the user: OAuth client credentials for partners, API keys only for the sandbox, mutual TLS deferred to a later phase, 'partner app' added to the glossary, and the rate-limit item will inherit the per-client identity. Post the resolution and close it.
evals.expected_output: The resolution comment states the agreed result as a table (OAuth client credentials for partners, API keys for the sandbox), then lists out of scope, deferred (mutual TLS), glossary changes ('partner app') and what later items inherit (per-client identity for the rate-limit item). Then the Decisions-so-far pointer is added and the item closed.
expectations: The resolution comment gives the agreed result as a table
The resolution comment lists deferred items (mutual TLS) and glossary changes ('partner app')
The resolution comment says what later items inherit (the per-client identity for the rate-limit item)

evals.name: prototype-item-body-template
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind chart the notification-vendor effort. We interviewed it earlier in this session and it outgrew one sitting; destination confirmed: a PRD. I said yes to the proposed map. One item is a prototype: check that vendor Knock can send a templated email and an in-app message from one API call, falling back to Courier if it cannot. Create that item.
evals.expected_output: The prototype item's body follows the prototype template: what to prove (one API call sends both a templated email and an in-app message), numbered pass checks, the action on fail, and the fallback (Courier). It carries the wayfind: prototype label and says whether it is logic or UI; the body does not state the type.
expectations: The prototype item body states what the prototype must prove
The body lists pass checks that can be judged passed or failed
The body names the action on fail and the fallback, Courier

evals.name: human-only-task-routes-to-wizard-and-records-no-values
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work 'Map: notification vendor' (#500). The claimed item 'Set up the Knock sandbox account' (#507, wayfind: task) needs someone to sign up in Knock's dashboard and create an API key; I'll do it. Work it.
evals.expected_output: The task is work only a human can do, so it routes to /wizard:generate for a guided script the user runs. The resolution comment records the names and locations of what was set up (the Knock sandbox account, the API key's name and where it is stored) and never the key's value.
expectations: Output routes the item to /wizard:generate rather than attempting the sign-up itself
The resolution records the names and locations of what was set up
Output does not ask for or record the API key's value

evals.name: prototype-files-on-dossier-folder-and-safe-push
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work 'Map: notification vendor' (#500). The claimed prototype item 'Prove Knock sends email and in-app from one call' (#504) is done: the pressure-test passed all checks. Another session is writing research findings to the same map's dossier branch right now. Save the prototype files and close the item.
evals.expected_output: The prototype's files go in #504's own folder on the map's single dossier branch. The push is fetch, rebase, then a plain push without force, retried after a fresh fetch and rebase if rejected; it needs no force because the other session writes only its own item's folder. The verdict (each pass check passed) goes in the resolution comment with a link to the folder; then the pointer is added and the item closed.
expectations: Output puts the prototype files in the item's own folder on the map's dossier branch, not a new branch per item
Output pushes with fetch, rebase and a plain non-force push, retrying on rejection
Output does not force-push
The resolution comment carries the prototype's verdict

evals.name: map-does-not-close-with-fog-left
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work 'Map: billing overhaul' (#200). Every decision item is closed and the frontier is empty, but Not-yet-specified still has one bullet: '**Tax display**: something about how taxes show on invoices feels unsettled'. Close the map.
evals.expected_output: The map does not close while Not-yet-specified holds a bullet. It posts no closing comment and does not close the map in this turn.
expectations: Output does not close the map while the Tax display bullet remains
Output offers a mop-up interview item for the bullet
Output offers an explicit out-of-scope ruling that would move the bullet to Out-of-scope with a reason
Output does not move the bullet to Out-of-scope on its own

evals.name: build-set-closes-to-plan-and-keeps-dossier-branch
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work 'Map: module extraction' (#600). Destination: a set of build items for the first module extraction. Every item is closed, the frontier and Not-yet-specified are empty, and the map has a dossier branch, dossier/600-module-extraction. The decisions are architectural choices, not yet a list of slices. Close the map and hand it on.
evals.expected_output: The closing comment states every decision in full and names the dossier branch. The map closes to /planning:plan, with the decisions as its task description, then /work-items:decompose from that plan, not straight to decompose, since the decisions do not yet read as slices. The dossier branch is kept until the destination's container closes, not deleted at map close.
expectations: Output hands the decisions to /planning:plan first, then /work-items:decompose from the plan
The closing comment names the dossier branch dossier/600-module-extraction
Output does not delete the dossier branch when the map closes

evals.name: provisional-decision-reversed-by-failed-prototype
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work 'Map: notification vendor' (#500). Decisions-so-far has 'Pick the vendor' (#502): Knock, provisional until 'Prove Knock sends email and in-app from one call' (#504). The claimed prototype #504 just failed: in-app messages need a second call. The prototype's fallback is Courier. Graduate #504.

Because the vendor decision rested on that prototype, the failure reverses it through the supersede sweep: a new decision item linking #502 opens, starting from the Courier fallback, #502 is not reopened or edited, and its Decisions-so-far line will point at the superseding decision once that resolves.
expectations: Output treats the Knock decision as reversed by the failed prototype rather than left standing
Output opens a new decision item that links #502 instead of reopening #502 or editing its resolution comment
Output names Courier, the fallback, as the new item's starting point

evals.name: ui-prototype-item-routes-to-explore-directions
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work 'Map: notification vendor' (#500). The claimed item 'Settle the channel mute controls' (#506) carries the wayfind: prototype label. Its body reads: '**Prove:** UI: a settings screen where a user mutes email, push and in-app per notification type reads clearly at a glance. **Pass checks:** 1.
